formal_statement: ∀ (n k : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → (∀ W : Submodule ℂ (Fin n × Fin n → ℂ), (∀ x ∈ W, ∑ i, x i ^ 2 = 0) → (∀ x ∈ W, ∑ i, x i ^ 3 = 0) → Module.finrank ℂ W ≤ k) → ∀ L : Submodule ℂ (Fin (n + 1) × Fin (n + 1) → ℂ), (∀ t ∈ L, MvPolynomial.eval ((fun p : Fin (n + 1) × Fin (n + 1) => if p.1.val = 0 ∧ p.2.val = 0 then 1 - ((n : ℂ) + 1) else 1) + t) (PEqualNP.Gct.permPoly ℂ (n + 1)) = 0) → Module.finrank ℂ L ≤ 4 * n + k
plain_statement: Let Sigma = J - m E_11 (a zero of perm_m, m = n+1 >= 3). If every linear space of n x n matrices on which sum t_ij^2 and sum t_ij^3 vanish has dim <= k, then every linear L with perm(Sigma + t) = 0 on L has dim <= 4n + k. Proof: cut L by the first row and column (2m-1) and by double centering (2m-4); on doubly centred t' the k = 2, 3 Taylor parts are (1/2) sum t^2 and (2/3) sum t^3.
title: Reduction at Sigma_m: l(Sigma_m) <= 4(m-1) + F, F the largest dim of a space of (m-1)x(m-1) matrices killing both power sums of the entries
